title: LiteLLM authenticated users can change proxy configuration and execute code
summary: The proxy configuration update endpoint lacks an administrator role check. An authenticated user can register Python handlers for code execution, read server files and overwrite account configuration.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.

severity.rationale: Authenticated code execution and file disclosure threaten shared agent gateways. An existing account or key is a meaningful but commonly met prerequisite.

exposure: Requires authenticated access to the LiteLLM proxy. This is an authorization flaw, not an unauthenticated access claim.

remediation.details: Use 1.83.0 or later, which requires proxy_admin for configuration updates. Until upgraded, restrict API key distribution; the vendor lists no configuration workaround.
remediation.risk: Updating can interrupt gateway requests; test dependent integrations.

verification: Confirm the running proxy uses litellm 1.83.0 or later and non-administrator access cannot update configuration.
